page: Microsoft Azure F8ads_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores running at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 vCPU-to-thread allocation. Its hardware configuration includes 32 MB of Level 3 cache, 32.0 GB of system memory delivering 4.0 GB per core, and an integrated 945 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. Hardware virtualization runs under Microsoft Hyper-V, and the CPU exposes vector acceleration extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-threaded execution performance, placing in the top decile for stress-ng single-core compute workloads, single-threaded gzip compression at 39.48 GB/sec, and bzip3 decompression at 17.87 GB/sec. Small language model token generation using a 135M model also achieved top-tier throughput at 358.88 tokens per second. In contrast, multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into middle-tier bands, with multi-core stress-ng reaching 29,294.17 and PassMark CPU overall scoring 24,323.24.

The bundled fast NVMe storage and dedicated core clock frequency make this instance suitable for workloads that require single-thread processing speed alongside fast temporary scratch space. Ideal deployments include batch compression, continuous integration build agents, low-latency microservices, static web traffic handling, and modest analytical or database caching tiers like Redis.
description: Microsoft Azure F8ads_v7 is a compute-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated x86_64 cores from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM and 945 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage. Lacking GPU acceleration, the system relies on high single-core compute performance supported by AVX-512 vector instruction sets. Benchmark evaluations confirm top-tier velocity in single-threaded operations, including gzip compression and single-core stress processing, while multi-threaded tasks and aggregate memory throughput remain in median performance tiers. The configuration offers balanced resource efficiency for compute-focused tasks requiring swift local storage IOPS. Best-fit use cases include CI/CD build environments, batch data compression, web application serving, Redis caching nodes, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
